in_text_mentions: ticed at the age of two and five, mental retardation, pes cavus, talipes equinovarus, clinodactyly, eczema, inverted cilia of the eye, strabismus and reduced hearing. panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Real patient clinical photograph of the affected right upper limb/shoulder/neck region under ambient room lighting. The Blaschko-linear hypopigmentation is subtle and was reported as not visible under ambient light, but the panel is part of the compound figure demonstrating the HI manifestation and its diagnostic subtlety. B: Real patient Wood's lamp photograph clearly showing streaked hypopigmentation along lines of Blaschko on the right arm/shoulder/neck, consistent with hypomelanosis of Ito. Skin tone not assessable under Wood's lamp illumination.

panels.rationale: Single posterior clinical photograph from a case report titled 'Hypomelanosis of Ito presenting with pediatric orthopedic issues'; the caption explicitly attributes the back skin pattern, scoliosis and leg-length discrepancy to this patient. The visible Blaschko-linear hypopigmented skin pattern and spinal/pelvic asymmetry are specific manifestations of hypomelanosis of Ito. The stated 2 cm leg-length discrepancy is clinically present but is not represented by a vocabulary finding key, so it is placed in proposed_findings rather than mapped to hemihypertrophy.

panels.figure_caption: Patient’s back: our patient seen from the back showing the skin pattern, leg length discrepancy of 2 centimetres and scoliosis.
in_text_mentions: ticed at the age of two and five, mental retardation, pes cavus, talipes equinovarus, clinodactyly, eczema, inverted cilia of the eye, strabismus and reduced hearing. He later developed a ventral hernia, which regressed, he got glomerulonephritis with proteinuria at the age of seven and, at the same time, it was discovered that there were missing testicles in both scrota. At the present time, he is 13 years old and has developed leg length discrepancy (Figure 4), back pain and a syrinx corresponding to the conus as well as scoliosis (Figure 5), for which he has recently had successful surgery.
